# RFC-0006: Framework Integration Protocol

> **Version:** 0.17.0 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** impl
> **Owners:** @Zihua Wu

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0006:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0006c-summary"></a>

This RFC governs framework integration protocol version 9: the boundary between InferLab and independently released integration packages, separate Engine, Gateway, and P/D Router planning, fused P/D frontend binding, concrete process rendering, one-shot operation behavior, generated wire projections, integration selection, and workspace-side package distribution. [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md) holds the specification overview and authority map.

*Since: v0.1.0*

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0006:C-INTEGRATIONS] Framework Integration Boundary (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-integrations"></a>

Framework-specific server-setting validation, logical lowering, command rendering, capability and environment probes, framework readiness, and server-specific control actions MUST remain outside the framework-neutral control plane.

Reusable framework integrations MUST be independently distributable and selected through the committed workspace dependency authority.

InferLab MUST distribute the adapter SDK and framework integration packages as wheels. The adapter SDK and each framework integration MUST own its package version independently of the InferLab product and other workspace-side packages. Releasing one workspace-side package MUST NOT require changing the InferLab product version or an unrelated workspace-side package version. A workspace-side package release MUST publish that distribution wheel to the package index. After the InferLab v0.8.0 product Release has been published, a package-only publication MUST NOT create a package-scoped GitHub tag or Release.

For each InferLab product release after v0.8.0, its tagged source snapshot MUST declare one closed workspace-side package inventory. Every adapter SDK or framework integration distribution in that snapshot MUST appear exactly once in the inventory, and product-owned measurement runners and SDKs MUST NOT appear. Each inventory entry MUST resolve to exactly one package `pyproject.toml`; its `[project].name` and `[project].version` values MUST be the distribution identity and version selected by that snapshot. Each integration MUST declare an exact dependency on the adapter SDK package version it was built and tested against.

For each InferLab product release after v0.8.0, the GitHub Release for that product version MUST use the tag `v<product-version>`, where `<product-version>` equals the product version in the tagged source snapshot. The Release MUST attach the product binaries, installer, embedded agent plugin, and LICENSE.

For every entry in the tagged workspace-side package inventory, the Release MUST attach exactly one wheel whose distribution identity and version match that entry and whose complete bytes equal the wheel published by the package index for that identity and version. The package index MUST expose exactly one such wheel; zero or multiple matching wheels MUST fail release preparation. The Release MUST attach one checksum asset named `<wheel-filename>.sha256` beside each wheel. Its contents MUST be exactly the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the complete wheel bytes, two ASCII spaces, the wheel filename, and one trailing newline. The computed digest MUST equal the package index reported SHA-256 digest. A missing inventory entry, package metadata, index wheel, index digest, wheel asset, checksum asset, or any identity, count, byte, or digest mismatch MUST fail release preparation before the product tag is created.

The complete set of wheel and checksum assets MUST be the Release inventory for workspace-side packages: it MUST contain every inventory entry exactly once and MUST contain no workspace-side distribution absent from the tagged inventory. Co-location under the product tag MUST NOT imply package-version equality or replace protocol-version and workspace-lock compatibility authority.

The existing v0.8.0 product tag and Release, its package-scoped tags and Releases, and every registry artifact published for that release MUST remain unchanged. They MUST NOT be deleted, moved, retagged, yanked, replaced, or have their published assets altered.

A committed workspace manifest MUST reference each workspace-side package by exact version or by an in-workspace filesystem path for development. A pinned version MAY resolve from an index or an in-workspace find-links location. Every filesystem reference MUST remain inside the workspace. The binary MUST NOT embed or materialize workspace-side integration content. A selected integration absent from the committed dependency set MUST fail before workflow effect naming the missing package.

Every integration operation MUST use a strict, versioned, operation-specific JSON request and response. Protocol version 9 is the sole contract for the Engine-role, Gateway, P/D Router, frontend-binding, placement, and rendering shapes in this RFC. Package-version equality MUST NOT be required as an additional runtime compatibility condition.

An integration MUST validate protocol version before request shape. An unsupported version MUST produce an unsupported-protocol-version error naming received and supported versions. The control plane MUST surface both versions and the remedy: update workspace adapter pins and relock, or use an InferLab release that speaks the installed integration's protocol. The control plane version output MUST state the adapter protocol version it speaks, so operators can check the correspondence before execution. Protocol version 8 input or output MUST NOT be partially interpreted as protocol version 9.

Protocol version 9 MUST carry the effective capture mechanism in `plan_serve` and `render_serve` requests whenever profiling is requested, the declared capture mechanism of each capture target, and the control-plane-assigned persistent trace directory on each model-rank allocation belonging to an engine-trace capture target under [RFC-0004:C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-workload-profiling). An adapter advertising protocol version 8 or earlier MUST NOT emit or consume these members.

Protocol version 9 MUST carry the synthetic acceptance declaration in `plan_serve` and `render_serve` requests whenever the serve declaration carries synthetic acceptance under [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-SYNTHETIC-ACCEPTANCE](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-serve-synthetic-acceptance): the explicit acceptance length for the explicit form, or the digest-verified curve text with its digest, model key, and effective thinking mode for the curve form. The plan response MUST return the effective acceptance length when the declaration is present. An adapter advertising protocol version 8 or earlier MUST NOT emit or consume these members.

A local one-shot operation MUST read one complete JSON request from stdin, write one complete JSON response and no other content to stdout, and write diagnostics to stderr.

Dedicated Rust wire DTOs MUST be the sole editable source of protocol representation. InferLab MUST generate a pinned Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema from the Rust deserialization contract and generate Pydantic v2 models from that schema. Generated schema and models MUST identify their source and MUST be checked for staleness. They MUST NOT be edited independently.

Framework settings MUST cross as structured data. Unknown fields MUST be rejected. Open framework parameters are allowed only in an explicitly named settings escape hatch, whose exact effective contents MUST be returned and recorded.

`plan_serve` MUST receive a logical `model` object containing exactly `id` and `served_name`. It MUST NOT receive a model-weight locator, machine, device, rank, port, cache path, or other placement fact.

`plan_serve` MUST receive the topology's requested canonical model-serving roles, replica counts, per-role settings, per-role parallelism patches, independently selected `gateway_backend` and `pd_router_backend` values when applicable, KV-transfer selection when applicable, readiness inputs, and, when profiling is requested, the effective capture mechanism selected under [RFC-0004:C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-workload-profiling).

Protocol-v9 frontend effective settings MUST be derived by the selected integration from the selected backend identities, topology, target and endpoint requirements, other explicitly named `plan_serve` inputs, and versioned integration defaults. Common Engine settings and per-model-role settings MUST NOT feed Gateway or P/D Router settings. Server configuration MUST NOT declare component-scoped Gateway or P/D Router settings in this RFC version.

`plan_serve` MUST preserve every requested model-serving role identity and replica count. It MUST NOT add, remove, rename, or resize those roles. It MUST preserve each requested frontend backend identity and MUST NOT infer an omitted backend or replace one backend selection from the other.

`plan_serve` MUST return the observed framework identity and version and, for every Engine role, its canonical identity, declared and effective replica count, complete effective settings, complete effective parallelism, whole-replica `device_count`, required ports and endpoint kinds, readiness, profiler controls with each capture target's declared capture mechanism, server-control actions, directed links, and declared render inputs when applicable.

Each public endpoint contract returned for a direct Engine or Gateway MUST carry an optional `server_metrics` member. When present, `server_metrics` MUST be an object containing exactly the required string member `path` and the optional string member `port`. Omission of `port` MUST select the public serving port. Presence of `port` MUST select the named port with that exact name on the concrete process that owns the public workload endpoint: the Gateway process when Gateway applies, or the rank-zero process of the direct public Engine replica. The selected name MUST be non-empty and MUST match exactly one port declared by that process. An empty, duplicate, unknown, or other-process name MUST be rejected before allocation. Presence of `server_metrics` MUST mean that the selected integration and topology expose an AIPerf-compatible endpoint on the public endpoint's protocol and host. `path` MUST be an absolute URL path and MUST NOT contain a scheme, authority, query, fragment, credential, concrete host, or allocated port. Omission of `server_metrics` MUST mean that InferLab has no qualified server-metrics capability for that endpoint.

The integration MUST own the framework-specific path and logical port selection. After endpoint allocation, the control plane MUST derive the exact metrics URL once from the accepted public protocol and host, selected public or named port, and declared path. The immutable resolved execution object MUST preserve `path`, the optional logical `port` selection, and that exact URL. Measurement execution MUST consume the frozen URL without reconstructing it. A Bench request for server metrics MUST NOT cause the control plane to guess `/metrics`, probe alternative paths or ports, or infer support from framework identity. Protocol version 9 MUST carry the optional `server_metrics` object through the generated Rust and Python projections and endpoint validation. Record projection is governed by RFC-0005:C-EVIDENCE, and measurement projection is governed by RFC-0004:C-MEASUREMENTS.

Each profiling capture target that advertises framework-range window control under [RFC-0004:C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-workload-profiling) MUST declare one capture-window control binding.

The binding MUST select exactly one logical HTTP endpoint shared by its start and stop actions: the entry endpoint of that target replica or the separately planned Gateway endpoint.

The binding MUST declare its start and stop actions as typed HTTP actions.

Each capture-window HTTP action MUST declare `method` and `path`. `method` MUST be exactly `post`. `path` MUST be an absolute origin path beginning with one `/` and MUST NOT contain a scheme, authority, query, fragment, credential, concrete host, allocated port, backslash, ASCII control character, or ASCII whitespace. The control plane MUST reject an invalid action before accepting the plan and MUST compose the effective URL from the accepted logical endpoint and declared path.

A capture-window HTTP action MAY carry one optional `body` member. When present, `body` MUST be a JSON object whose complete contents are declared by the integration. The control plane MUST serialize that exact object as the request payload and send `Content-Type: application/json`. An absent `body` MUST send no request payload and MUST NOT be inferred as an empty object.

Framework-specific window-control inputs MUST remain in that typed action. The control plane MUST execute the declared action without inferring a framework default or branching on framework identity. It MUST apply the profiling deadline owned by RFC-0004:C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING, MUST NOT follow redirects, and MUST treat only a received 2xx response as success. Serialization, transport, deadline, invalid-response, redirect, and other non-2xx outcomes MUST fail the attempted action.

The control plane MUST reject a plan response that selects a Gateway endpoint when the plan has no Gateway before accepting that response.

The control plane MUST resolve the selected logical endpoint only after frontend composition and model-rank decomposition.

Dry-run output MUST preserve the declared endpoint selection, typed actions including body presence and contents, resolved control process, and effective action URLs. Execution evidence is governed by RFC-0005:C-EVIDENCE.

The capture target process and capture-window control process MAY differ.

An integration MUST NOT return a concrete process identity, host, port, or URL as the logical capture-window endpoint.

Protocol version 9 MUST carry this required binding and each action's optional `body` member without a protocol-8 compatibility interpretation.

When Gateway applies, `plan_serve` MUST return one separate Gateway result containing the selected backend identity, implementation identity and observable version, complete effective settings, public endpoint contract, public readiness, public server controls, target requirements, render inputs, and `render_source`. When P/D Router applies, it MUST return one separate P/D Router result containing the selected backend identity, implementation identity and observable version, complete effective settings, routing policies, complete target semantics, bootstrap and registry requirements, internal handoff contract, readiness, render inputs, and `render_source`.

`render_source` MUST be exactly `control_plane` or `integration` and MUST mean only which side renders an accepted concrete frontend allocation. It MUST NOT represent provider identity, process ownership, placement authority, endpoint authority, lifecycle authority, cleanup authority, or record authority.

A direct `single` plan MUST omit both frontend results. A routed `single` plan MUST return Gateway and omit P/D Router. A `prefill_decode` plan MUST return both results.

For `prefill_decode`, both component plans MUST name the same rendering source and compatible co-rendering requirements. The control plane, not the integration response, MUST derive the closed `[gateway, pd_router]` binding.

`plan_serve` MUST NOT return a server-wide effective parallelism shape. It MUST NOT select model rank counts, concrete processes, machines, devices, model locators, endpoint values, runtime storage, or a readiness deadline.

After planning, the control plane MUST choose concrete model-rank decomposition and derive the one frontend process when Gateway applies, then resolve placement, per-machine model locators, ports, cache paths, network facts, and process identities.

Every concrete allocation supplied to `render_serve` MUST be either one model-rank allocation or one frontend allocation. A model-rank allocation MUST contain `process`, `role`, `replica`, `rank`, `rank_count`, `machine`, ordered nonempty `devices`, required per-rank `model_locator`, optional `endpoint`, allocated `ports`, `cache`, `launch`, the control-plane-assigned persistent trace directory when the rank belongs to an engine-trace capture target, resolved role settings and parallelism, links and dependencies needed for rendering, and control-plane-supplied render inputs.

A frontend allocation MUST contain `process`, canonical `process_role`, one closed ordered `components` value of `[gateway]` or `[gateway, pd_router]`, `machine`, an empty device list, no model locator, its public endpoint, allocated `ports`, `cache`, `launch`, the accepted component plans, links and dependencies needed for rendering, and control-plane-supplied render inputs.

`[gateway]` MUST represent only a routed-single Gateway. `[gateway, pd_router]` MUST represent only a fused P/D frontend. The component value MUST NOT be open or unordered, and `process_role` MUST be `gateway` for both bindings.

`render_serve` MUST receive every model-rank allocation and every frontend allocation whose accepted `render_source` is `integration`. It MUST NOT receive a control-plane-rendered frontend allocation. A P/D frontend MUST be supplied once, only when both component plans name the same integration rendering source.

`render_serve` MUST return exactly one rendered process for every supplied allocation and no additional process. Each rendered model process MUST preserve process, role, replica, rank, and rank-count identity. Each rendered frontend process MUST preserve process, process-role, and component binding. A rendered process MAY return integration-rendered launch files under [RFC-0006:C-LAUNCH-FILES](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-launch-files).

The control plane MUST reject missing, duplicate, extra, rebound, or component-mismatched rendered processes and MUST validate every integration response semantically before accepting it for execution.

The control plane MUST retain authority for component composition, local and remote placement, model-rank decomposition, process and frontend lifecycle, endpoint allocation and ownership, runtime storage, profiler lifecycle, timeout, cancellation, cleanup, measurement orchestration, and authoritative records.

A framework integration MUST NOT own a long-running lifecycle, execute an ordinary Eval or Bench client, write authoritative InferLab records, or define an arbitrary task or shell-command operation. The protocol MUST NOT define `LowerEval` or `LowerBench`.

Protocol-relevant records MUST preserve integration package identity, protocol version, framework identity, planning and rendering request and response digests, both frontend backend identities when present, the closed component binding when present, each rendering source, and effective rendered commands.

**Rationale:** Protocol version 7 keeps two-phase planning and rendering while replacing the overloaded routing-ownership union with explicit Gateway and P/D Router component plans. Independent backend identities express separate experimental choices; `render_source` states only the lowering boundary. The two closed frontend bindings encode routed single and the currently demonstrated fused P/D process without restoring a universal deployment graph. Generated projections keep Rust wire DTOs authoritative across languages, while exact wheel pins make the workspace revision authoritative for adapter behavior. Protocol version 8 adds the capture-mechanism selection and engine-trace trace storage so workload-attached engine profilers share the same two-phase boundary without the control plane learning framework profiler spellings. Protocol version 9 adds the synthetic acceptance overlay so framework-specific injection spelling and the keyed golden-curve lookup stay with the owning integration — where the operator's speculative configuration supplies the draft count — while the control plane retains curve integrity, resolved-value validation, and evidence authority under [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-SYNTHETIC-ACCEPTANCE](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-serve-synthetic-acceptance).

A logical capture-window endpoint lets the integration state whether an Engine replica or Gateway exposes the framework action while InferLab remains authoritative for concrete process and endpoint allocation. Keeping that binding on the capture target identifies which action controls which trace without turning the Gateway into a capture target or introducing a general component graph. The optional JSON body keeps framework-specific control semantics in the integration-owned action while the control plane retains generic HTTP execution and evidence authority. Protocol version 7 remains an unreleased candidate; requiring every generated projection and maintained integration to adopt this binding in that candidate preserves protocol-version compatibility instead of publishing incompatible protocol-v7 shapes.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0006:C-LAUNCH-FILES] Integration-Rendered Launch Files (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-launch-files"></a>

`plan_serve` MAY declare workspace-authored UTF-8 text files that the integration requires as inputs to final rendering.

Each render-input declaration MUST identify exactly one source path.

The control plane MUST read each declared source path once and MUST supply its path, exact UTF-8 text, and SHA-256 digest to final rendering.

A relative render-input path MUST resolve from the workspace root.

An unreadable or non-UTF-8 render input MUST fail resolution before any process launches.

An integration that declares a render input MUST consume the control-plane-supplied text during final rendering and MUST NOT reopen that source path from its own execution environment.

Process-backed, built-image-backed, and external-image-backed adapter realizations MUST receive identical render-input contents for the same resolved workspace state.

An image-backed adapter realization MUST receive only the declared render-input contents and MUST NOT require a workspace or containing-directory mount solely to render a launch file.

`render_serve` MAY declare immutable text files required to launch a rendered process when the framework accepts required effective configuration only through a file input.

Each launch-file declaration MUST belong to exactly one rendered process.

Each launch-file declaration MUST contain the exact UTF-8 text, its SHA-256 digest, and a normalized relative path below that process's control-plane-allocated runtime-cache root.

The SHA-256 digest MUST be computed over the file's UTF-8 encoded bytes.

The declared relative path MUST have the form `launch-files/<sha256>/<name>`, where `<sha256>` is the complete lowercase hexadecimal content digest and `<name>` is one nonempty path component.

A launch-file relative path MUST NOT be absolute or escape its allocated runtime-cache root.

A rendered process invocation that consumes a launch file MUST reference the path formed from the control-plane-supplied runtime-cache root and the declared relative path.

Before accepting integration output, the control plane MUST validate the process binding, path confinement, content digest, and digest-bearing relative path of every declared launch file.

Dry-run MUST preserve each launch file's resolved path, exact text, and content digest without materializing the file.

Before spawning a process that owns launch files, InferLab MUST materialize their exact text on that process's launch machine.

InferLab MUST publish launch-file bytes atomically.

An existing launch-file target MAY be reused only when its bytes match the declared digest.

A published launch-file target MUST NOT be truncated or replaced.

A process MUST NOT observe launch-file bytes whose digest differs from its declaration.

A containerized substitution MUST expose each materialized launch file to the process at the same resolved path recorded in the command.

A launch-file materialization failure MUST fail that process before spawn and MUST NOT create a runtime handle for it.

Execution records MUST preserve each launch file's resolved path, exact text, and content digest with the rendered process that consumed it.

Render-input files and integration-rendered launch files are machine-local runtime inputs. They MUST NOT enter an image build context, image contents, or another portable artifact merely because a runtime process consumes them.

Render-input and launch-file declarations in these required request and response shapes MUST use adapter protocol version 9. An adapter advertising protocol version 8 or earlier MUST NOT emit or consume them.

**Rationale:** Some framework entry points accept dynamic effective configuration only through files whose contents depend on allocated endpoints, and some of those files must preserve operator-authored framework settings. Keeping the integration authoritative for framework-specific composition while assigning source-file access, target-machine materialization, dry-run, lifecycle ordering, and evidence to the control plane preserves the integration boundary in [RFC-0006:C-INTEGRATIONS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-integrations). Passing only declared source text makes rendering independent of whether the adapter runs as a workspace process or inside a serving image and avoids exposing the surrounding workspace to that image. Digest-bearing paths and atomic publication let concurrent runs safely reuse identical rendered text without exposing partial or mismatched content, while retaining the exact output text keeps file-only settings on the same evidence plane as command arguments and environment values. The existing runtime-cache root is known during final rendering and is already projected consistently across local, SSH, and containerized launches. These local runtime inputs are deliberately separate from the portable artifact boundary governed by [RFC-0007](../rfc/RFC-0007.md).

*Since: v0.5.0*

### [RFC-0006:C-OPENAI-ENDPOINT-CONTRACT] OpenAI Endpoint Contract (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-openai-endpoint-contract"></a>

The public endpoint requirement returned by `plan_serve` MUST contain exactly one protocol plus one named completions path and one named chat-completions path.

Both named paths MUST be absolute HTTP paths. They MUST begin with `/`. They MUST NOT contain a scheme, authority, query, fragment, empty path segment, `.` segment, or `..` segment. They MUST NOT end with `/`.

For the OpenAI-compatible serving workflows governed by [RFC-0003:C-OPENAI-WORKLOAD-ROUTES](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-openai-workload-routes), the completions path MUST equal `/v1/completions` and the chat-completions path MUST equal `/v1/chat/completions`.

The endpoint requirement MUST NOT retain a singular generic API path. A client request MUST carry both named path facts even when that client uses only one of them.

For direct `single`, the accepted `serve` Engine result MUST supply the public endpoint requirement. For every Gateway-backed topology, the Gateway result MUST supply it. A P/D Router result MUST NOT supply or replace the public endpoint requirement.

Every maintained integration MUST return both named paths for every direct Engine endpoint and Gateway backend it supports.

The control plane MUST reject a plan response with a missing or extra endpoint member, a path other than the exact required value, equal named paths, or a public endpoint attached to P/D Router before any serving process launches. After accepting the plan response, the resolved endpoint, every measurement-client input, dry-run output, and execution record MUST preserve both path strings exactly; no later layer may replace either accepted value.

Protocol version 9 MUST carry this endpoint shape in `plan_serve` responses, resolved client inputs, generated schema and Pydantic models, cross-language fixtures, dry-run output, and records. Protocol version 8 input or output MUST NOT be partially interpreted as protocol version 9.

**Rationale:** One generic path cannot be the authority for both chat generation and completions scoring. Gateway is the sole public route authority whenever present; P/D Router remains an internal orchestration component. Strict path validation keeps the selected integration authoritative for route facts without allowing it to replace control-plane-owned host or port values.

*Since: v0.8.1*
